detail.returnBasisStock: The overview, chart, and return calendar use adjusted closes. The stock annual cash-return table below uses unadjusted closes and adds after-tax cash dividends separately. CAGR (compound annual growth rate) converts the period's total return into an equivalent compounded yearly growth rate using actual elapsed days; it is not the return earned in every calendar year.
detail.returnBasisAdjusted: The overview, chart, and return calendar use adjusted closes. CAGR (compound annual growth rate) converts the period's total return into an equivalent compounded yearly growth rate using actual elapsed days; it is not the return earned in every calendar year.
detail.qualityDescription: Daily win rate, downside risk, and rolling one-year outcomes complement point-in-time CAGR and max drawdown.
detail.qualityNote: All metrics use adjusted closes. Downside volatility counts returns below 0%; Sortino uses a 0% target; rolling one-year returns are calculated for every eligible daily endpoint.
detail.fundamentalsDescription: Only stock or ETF valuation and market fields available from the current data source are shown.
detail.fundamentalsHistoryDescription: P/E and P/B are quarterly valuation ratios; ROE is annual. Use them to compare the current reading with its own history.

stockCompare.title: US Stock Compare
stockCompare.methodologyReturn: Price return: calculated from the prior year-end to the current year-end close, excluding cash dividends.
stockCompare.methodologyDividend: After-tax dividend yield: annual cash dividend per share × (1 − tax rate) ÷ prior year-end close.
stockCompare.methodologyCombined: Annual combined return (after tax): price return plus after-tax dividend yield; it assumes no dividend reinvestment and is not a multi-year CAGR.
stockCompare.methodologyDrawdown: Max drawdown: the largest close-to-close peak-to-subsequent-trough decline within a calendar year.
stockCompare.methodologyCurrentYear: Current-year metrics are year-to-date (YTD) and are not annualized projections.
stockCompare.methodologyCache: Yahoo daily prices and ex-dividend events are used; successful results are cached for 6 hours and failures for 5 minutes.

vix.tipExtremeCalm: Let profits run; take partial profits. Avoid chasing highs.
vix.tipLowVol: Light positions on the right side; wait on the left. Avoid chasing.
vix.tipNormal: Mean reversion — stick to your plan. Stay the course with DCA.
vix.tipFear: Market pullback — deploy reserves and buy in tranches.
vix.tipHighFear: Likely near a stage bottom — accumulate aggressively and increase DCA.
vix.tipExtremePanic: Historic buying opportunity! Buy aggressively but keep some powder dry.
vix.corrWeakening: SPY/VIX negative correlation weakening — watch for anomaly risk
vix.corrNormal: SPY/VIX still maintaining typical negative correlation
vix.ruleTip:
VIX Zones & Guidelines:
<12  Extreme Calm  ❌ Avoid chasing (let profits run / take partial profits)
12-15 Low Vol       ❌ Avoid chasing (light positions / wait on left)
15-20 Normal Range  ✅ Stay the course (mean reversion / stick to plan)
20-25 Fear Rising   ✅ Buy in tranches (market pullback / deploy reserves)
25-35 High Fear     ✅ Increase DCA (stage bottom / accumulate aggressively)
>=35 Extreme Panic  ✅ Aggressive buy (historic opportunity / keep powder dry)
vix.adviceVixTooltip: VIX is the CBOE Volatility Index, often called the Fear Index. It reflects the market's expectation of ~30-day volatility for the S&P 500. Higher values generally indicate greater market fear.
vix.adviceZoneTooltip: Based on the absolute VIX level: <12 Extreme Calm, 12-15 Low Volatility, 15-20 Normal Range, 20-25 Fear Rising, 25-30 High Fear, >30 Extreme Panic.
vix.advicePercentileTooltip: The historical position of the current VIX value among the past ~1 year of trading days. E.g., 79% means VIX was at or below the current level on ~79% of days — higher values = closer to 1-year highs.
vix.adviceCorrelationTooltip: The correlation coefficient between SPY daily returns and VIX daily returns over the last 30 trading days. Typically negative (SPY down → VIX up). Closer to -1 = stronger negative correlation; near 0 = weakening; positive = structural anomaly or risk signal.
vix.adviceTipTooltip: A qualitative note based on current VIX absolute level, 1-year percentile, and SPY/VIX 30-day correlation. For risk observation only — not investment advice.
vix.thresholdMethod: Every trading day whose close reaches the threshold is counted separately. Forward windows use 1, 5, 21, 126, and 252 trading sessions with adjusted SPY/QQQ closes. Incomplete windows near the end of the data are shown as unavailable.
vix.thresholdEmptyHint: Choose an index, threshold, and date range to begin.
vix.thresholdNoEvents: No trading days reached the threshold in this range.
vix.thresholdInvalidRange: End date cannot be earlier than start date.
vix.thresholdInvalidValue: Enter a valid threshold greater than 0.
